## F10.custom-command-format — Custom command format

Definition: File layout and frontmatter of a user command.
- claude-code [supported, verified] Custom commands are flat Markdown files in `.claude/commands/` whose filenames become command names; skills are their recommended successor. A command's frontmatter can name a `model` other than the session's, which makes that turn a model switch. In a plugin, `commands/‹file›.md` becomes `/‹plugin›:‹file›`; a subdirectory adds a segment. | ev: E-claude-code-00797, E-claude-code-12613, E-claude-code-12393
- codex-cli [partial, verified] Custom prompts are Markdown files invoked as slash commands in both the Codex CLI and the IDE extension. The description is set in YAML front matter as `description:` and shown under the command name in the popup; typing `/prompts:draftpr` shows the front-matter description and argument hints. | limit: Custom prompts are deprecated. They require explicit invocation and live in your local Codex home directory (for example, `~/.codex`), so they're not shared through your repository. | ev: E-codex-cli-03079, E-codex-cli-03082, E-codex-cli-03084, E-codex-cli-03080
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] Commands are individual .md files in .claude/commands/, and the command name is derived from the filename. Command files use a simplified format (no name field required) and support argument-hint, description, allowed-tools, and disable-model-invocation. Extensions can also add slash commands using the SDK that ships with the CLI. | ev: E-copilot-cli-03646, E-copilot-cli-01642
- copilot-vscode [partial, verified] Prompt files are Markdown files with the `.prompt.md` extension; an optional YAML frontmatter header configures the prompt's behavior. A prompt file can add the `agent` tool set to its `tools` frontmatter to delegate to subagents, and one documented example path is `.github/prompts/plan.prompt.md`. | limit: Prompt files are deprecated for Agent Host sessions and aren't loaded by Agent Host. They continue to work with the Local agent for now, but the Local agent will be removed in a future release. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00218, E-copilot-vscode-01006, E-copilot-vscode-00434, E-copilot-vscode-01739
- cursor [supported, unverified] Commands are reusable prompts invoked with `/` in Agent chat; they are markdown files that define a focused workflow or action. Custom commands are defined in a `.cursor/commands` directory. The plugin reference says commands support `.md`, `.mdc`, `.markdown` and `.txt` extensions and can include YAML frontmatter. | ev: E-cursor-00521, E-cursor-03513, E-cursor-03578
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] Custom slash commands are loaded from `.toml` files; an example file sets `description = "Generates a fix for a given issue."`. ## F10.arguments — Arguments

Definition: How a command receives arguments.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] A command file can accept parameters with `$ARGUMENTS`, as in `/fix-issue 123`. Built-in commands also take arguments: `/config` accepts `key=value` pairs to set a setting directly, and `/model`, `/effort`, `/fast`, `/color` and `/rename` accept the value as an argument, for example `/model sonnet` (those argument forms require Claude Code v2.1.205 or later). | ev: E-claude-code-06817, E-claude-code-07235, E-claude-code-09660
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Custom prompts expand positional placeholders `$1` through `$9` from space-separated arguments after the command; `$ARGUMENTS` includes them all. Named placeholders use uppercase names like `$FILE`, supplied as `KEY=value` (quote values with spaces). `argument-hint: KEY=‹value›` documents expected parameters. The built-in `/review` accepts trailing focus text. | ev: E-codex-cli-03086, E-codex-cli-03087, E-codex-cli-03085, E-codex-cli-02058
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] /review optionally takes a prompt, path, or file pattern to narrow the review scope, and instructions can be appended after /pr create. Command files support an argument-hint field, and over ACP each advertised command has an optional input.hint describing its arguments. | ev: E-copilot-cli-03647, E-copilot-cli-02705, E-copilot-cli-02827, E-copilot-cli-00832
- copilot-vscode [supported, verified] Extra text can follow a slash command in the chat input: `/create-react-form formName=MyForm` or `/create-api for listing customers` for prompt files, and `/webapp-testing for the login page` for skills. `/compact` accepts optional custom instructions after the command; in the Agents window, `/troubleshoot #session` selects a local or remote session before you add your question. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01760, E-copilot-vscode-01551, E-copilot-vscode-00379, E-copilot-vscode-00243
- cursor [supported, verified] Built-in commands take their argument after the command name: `/side` or `/btw` can be followed by your question in the chat input, and `/model [filter]` selects a model (press Tab to edit). | ev: E-cursor-01589, E-cursor-00335
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] Custom commands support two methods for handling arguments. In the main body of the prompt the `{{args}}` placeholder has the arguments injected exactly as given; under default argument handling the CLI appends the full command you typed to the end of the prompt. For MCP prompt slash commands the CLI automatically handles parsing arguments. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00212, E-gemini-cli-00213, E-gemini-cli-00052, E-gemini-cli-02294

## F10.discovery-paths — Discovery paths

Definition: Where custom commands are found, by scope.

When an added directory and the project both define a command with the same name, Claude Code runs the project's command. `/reload-skills` re-scans skill and command directories without restarting. | ev: E-claude-code-09451, E-claude-code-12392, E-claude-code-12210, E-claude-code-07295

## F10.command-skill-relation — Relation to skills

Definition: Whether commands and skills are the same mechanism.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] A file at `commands/deploy.md` creates `/deploy` the same way a skill at `skills/deploy/SKILL.md` does, and both can be auto-invoked by Claude. Skills use a directory with SKILL.md, letting you bundle supporting files alongside; skills are the recommended way to package multi-step commands. `--disable-slash-commands` disables all skills and commands for a session. | ev: E-claude-code-06815, E-claude-code-09451, E-claude-code-07044
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Custom prompts are deprecated and the docs point to skills instead. Enabled skills also appear in the slash command list alongside custom prompts. Slash commands imported from other agents map to Skills. | ev: E-codex-cli-03078, E-codex-cli-04341, E-codex-cli-04041
- copilot-cli [supported, verified] Commands are an alternative to skills, stored as individual .md files in .claude/commands/ in a simplified format (no name field required). Commands have lower priority than skills with the same name. Enabled, user-invocable skills appear as /SKILL-NAME commands. | ev: E-copilot-cli-03646, E-copilot-cli-00830, E-copilot-cli-03648
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] Skills and prompt files both appear as slash commands in chat, alongside each other: typing `/` lists them, and `/‹name›` invokes an agent skill or reusable prompt by name. Prompt files are also known as slash commands, and Migrate Prompt Files converts workspace and user prompt files to agent skills. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00541, E-copilot-vscode-01550, E-copilot-vscode-01747, E-copilot-vscode-01736
- cursor [supported, unverified] Skills can also be manually invoked by typing `/` in Agent chat. Setting `disable-model-invocation: true` makes a skill behave like a traditional slash command, included only when you explicitly type `/skill-name`. Built-in `/migrate-to-skills` (Cursor 2.4+) converts eligible rules and commands to skills; slash commands become skills with `disable-model-invocation: true`. | ev: E-cursor-03937, E-cursor-03955, E-cursor-04320, E-cursor-03897
